answer_1.quote: Facts in LLMs are often represented as triplets of (subject, relation, object), or (s, r, o) for short. Querying an LLM with a prompt p(s, r), where p expresses the relation r and contains the subject s (e.g., "In which city is the Brandenburg Gate located?"), should result in retrieving the object o (e.g., "Berlin"), provided that the fact (s, r, o) is known to the LLM.
answer_1.outputs: The paper evaluates how well LLMs retrieve factual knowledge before and after in-context knowledge edits, and after applying reversal tokens to counteract malicious edits

answer_2.quote: We calculate the matching accuracy, i.e., the agreement of the original output and the output of the edited prompt with reversal tokens.
